Record Class ChaosScenario

java.lang.Object
java.lang.Record
com.macstab.chaos.jvm.api.ChaosScenario
Record Components:
id - unique identifier surfaced in diagnostics, JMX, JFR events, and logs
description - human-readable description; null normalises to ""
scope - visibility scope; null defaults to ChaosScenario.ScenarioScope.JVM
selector - selects which JVM operations are eligible for chaos
effect - the chaos effect applied when the selector matches
activationPolicy - controls when and how often the effect fires
precedence - tie-breaker for conflicting terminal actions (higher wins)
tags - free-form metadata surfaced in diagnostics and JFR events
public record ChaosScenario(String id, String description, ChaosScenario.ScenarioScope scope, ChaosSelector selector, ChaosEffect effect, ActivationPolicy activationPolicy, int precedence, Map<String,String> tags) extends Record
Immutable description of a single chaos injection scenario.

A scenario binds three orthogonal concerns:

  • ChaosSelector — which JVM operations are eligible
  • ChaosEffect — what happens when a match occurs
  • ActivationPolicy — when and how often the effect fires

Scenarios are activated via ChaosControlPlane.activate(ChaosScenario), which returns a ChaosActivationHandle for lifecycle control. Multiple scenarios may be active simultaneously; when more than one matches an operation, all effects compose: delays sum, and the highest-precedence terminal action (reject, suppress, exception) wins.

Use builder(String) to construct instances: 

ChaosScenario scenario = ChaosScenario.builder("slow-redis")
    .description("Simulate a slow Redis connection under load")
    .selector(ChaosSelector.method(
        Set.of(OperationType.METHOD_ENTER),
        NamePattern.prefix("io.lettuce.core"),
        NamePattern.any()))
    .effect(ChaosEffect.delay(Duration.ofMillis(200), Duration.ofMillis(500)))
    .activationPolicy(ActivationPolicy.always())
    .build();

Scope: ChaosScenario.ScenarioScope.JVM scenarios intercept all matching operations in the JVM. ChaosScenario.ScenarioScope.SESSION scenarios intercept only operations on threads bound to a specific session, enabling per-test isolation in shared JVM environments.
